description: Root dir of persistent Docker state. Renaming an existing data-root requires daemon stop + manual move; the daemon doesn't migrate. Containerd image store keeps image layers under /var/lib/containerd regardless.
Root dir for runtime exec state files (container OCI bundles, etc.). On tmpfs by default — wiped on reboot, which is fine.
Daemon PID file. Set with `--pidfile` flag or daemon.json. Stale pidfile after crash can prevent restart — clean up if `dockerd` complains 'pid file found, ensure docker is not running'.
Group that owns the docker.sock unix socket. Membership grants effective root on the host (an attacker can mount / and chroot). Treat docker-group membership as sudo membership.

List of sockets the daemon listens on. e.g. ["unix:///var/run/docker.sock","tcp://127.0.0.1:2375"]. CONFLICTS with `-H` flag set via systemd unit's ExecStart — daemon refuses to start if both define hosts. Convention: 2375 = no TLS, 2376 = TLS.
Use TLS on TCP listeners. Implied by tlsverify.
Use TLS and verify the client (mTLS). Required for any production-grade exposed TCP socket.
CA cert that signed allowed client certs. With tlsverify, only certs chained from this CA are accepted.
Daemon's own TLS server cert.
Private key matching tlscert.

default_value: overlay2 (legacy installs); containerd snapshotter (29.0+ fresh installs)
description: Classic storage driver name. Switching mid-life renders existing local images/containers inaccessible — must `docker save` / push first. Values: overlay2, fuse-overlayfs, btrfs, zfs, vfs, windowsfilter.
Driver-specific options as `key=value` strings. See `storage-opts` scope below for the per-driver knobs.
Default container logging driver. `local` recommended for new installs (rotation by default). Existing containers don't pick up changes — must be re-created.
Default log-driver options. Keys depend on selected driver. ALL VALUES MUST BE STRINGS in JSON (booleans/numbers must be quoted: `"max-file": "3"`).

Keep containers running across daemon restart. Patch upgrades only (`YY.MM.x`); skipped major upgrades may break the reconnect. Daemon-options that change (bridge IP, graph driver) prevent the reconnect — containers must be stopped manually.

User-namespace remap. `default` uses the `dockremap` user; or specify `<user>` / `<user>:<group>`. Requires entries in /etc/subuid + /etc/subgid. Mutually exclusive with `--privileged`, `--ipc=host`, `--net=host`, `--pid=host` containers — those refuse to start when remap is on.
Daemon-managed iptables rules for NAT, isolation, port-publish. Disabling = no DNAT for `-p` published ports. Detail of chains in docker/networking.
Daemon-managed ip6tables rules. Required for IPv6 packet filtering and port mapping. Auto-loads `ip6_tables` kernel module on most distros; needs manual `modprobe ip6_tables` inside Docker-in-Docker.
Network bridge to attach containers to (default `docker0`). Detail in docker/networking. Setting to `none` disables the default bridge.
IPv4 address (with prefix) for the default bridge. e.g. `172.18.0.1/16`. Pinning avoids subnet collisions with VPNs / on-prem networks.
IPv6 address for the default bridge.
MTU of the default bridge. Lower (e.g. 1450) on hosts behind GRE/IPsec tunnels — without this, large packets are silently dropped (TCP works for small flows, breaks on >MTU writes).
IPv4 subnet for the default bridge network (must be within `bip`).
IPv6 subnet for the default bridge. e.g. `2001:db8:1::/64`. Required (with `ipv6: true`) for IPv6 on the default bridge.
Enable IPv6 on the default bridge. Linux-only.
Enable kernel `net.ipv4.ip_forward`. Disabling kills any cross-network routing — containers can't reach the internet through the bridge.
IP masquerading (SNAT) on the default bridge. Without this, container packets retain their internal IP, often filtered by external networks.
Inter-container communication on the default bridge. With `icc: false`, containers on the default bridge can't reach each other (must use user-defined network or explicit `--link`).

Use docker-proxy binary for loopback (host:container) traffic. Disabling pushes more work into iptables and may improve perf, but breaks some odd cases (port-publish from same container that originates the connection).
Path to the docker-proxy binary if you need a custom build.
Firewall backend: `iptables` or `nftables`. Pick `nftables` on modern systems where iptables is a compat wrapper.
DNS server(s) for containers. Overrides /etc/resolv.conf. Use `["8.8.8.8","1.1.1.1"]` to bypass a broken corporate resolver.
DNS search domains for containers.
resolv.conf options (e.g. `["ndots:1","timeout:2"]`). Critical for k8s-style cluster DNS performance.
IP pools for new user-defined networks. Configure to avoid clashes with on-prem subnets. Add IPv6 pools to use deterministic v6 ranges instead of ULA.
Default network driver options keyed by driver name. e.g. `{"bridge": {"com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade": "true"}}`.
IP addresses the special `host-gateway` token resolves to in `--add-host=host:host-gateway`. Defaults to default-bridge IPs. Used for containers reaching the host without baking 172.x.0.1.
In bridge networks, accept packets carrying this firewall mark/mask. Used for advanced policy routing setups.
Allow remote access to published ports on container IPs (skips standard iptables-based routing).
Parent cgroup all containers nest under. e.g. `system.slice/docker.slice` to integrate with systemd accounting.
Default cgroup-namespace mode for new containers (`host` or `private`). Private hides the host's cgroup tree from the container.
Default IPC mode (`shareable` or `private`). Private = the container has its own IPC namespace and can't be joined.
Default /dev/shm size for new containers. Bump for shared-memory-heavy workloads (Postgres, Chromium-headless).
Default ulimits for all new containers. e.g. `{"nofile":{"Name":"nofile","Soft":65536,"Hard":65536}}`. Common fix for 'too many open files' on busy services.
Inject docker-init as pid 1 by default for every container. Trades a tiny memory hit for correct signal-forward + zombie-reap.
Path to docker-init binary. Override only if you ship a custom init.
Set `no-new-privileges: true` by default for new containers. Equivalent to `--security-opt=no-new-privileges`. Forbids gaining new caps via setuid binaries — strong baseline hardening.
Default seccomp profile. `builtin` = Docker's default (~50 syscalls blocked). `unconfined` = no seccomp (do not). Or path to custom JSON profile.
Enable SELinux support; requires SELinux running in enforcing/permissive on the host. Detail in docker/security.
Default OCI runtime. Override per-container with `docker run --runtime <name>`.

Map of named runtimes. Two forms: drop-in (`{"path":"/path/to/binary"}`) for runc-compatible (e.g. youki); shim (`{"runtimeType":"io.containerd.runsc.v1"}`) for runtimes shipping their own containerd shim.
CLI form of `runtimes` map. e.g. `--add-runtime youki=/usr/local/bin/youki`. Equivalent to a single entry under `runtimes`.
Path to external containerd grpc socket. Setting it makes dockerd attach to a separately-managed containerd instead of starting one.
Containerd namespace dockerd uses for its containers/images.
Containerd namespace for plugins.
Start the bundled containerd with the CRI plugin (for Kubernetes integration).
Prometheus metrics endpoint. e.g. `127.0.0.1:9323`. Bound to loopback by default — exposing on `0.0.0.0` opens an info-leak surface.
Enable experimental features. Required for some metrics/feature combinations.
Named feature flags. e.g. `{"containerd-snapshotter": true}` to opt into the containerd image store on a legacy install.
Builder-related daemon config. Most active surface lives in BuildKit / buildkitd.toml; this key is a dockerd-side hook.
Daemon-side HTTP/HTTPS proxy + bypass list. Takes precedence over env vars. e.g. `{"http-proxy":"http://proxy.example.com:3128","no-proxy":"*.test.example.com,.example.org,127.0.0.0/8"}`.
CLI flag form: `--http-proxy`. Same as `proxies.http-proxy`.
HTTPS proxy URL.
Comma-separated NO_PROXY hosts/CIDRs.
List of preferred registry mirrors for Docker Hub pulls. e.g. `["https://mirror.gcr.io"]`.
Registries the daemon will talk to over HTTP / with self-signed TLS. e.g. `["localhost:5000","10.0.0.0/8"]`. Common for in-cluster pull-through caches.
Max parallel layer downloads per pull. Bump for large images on fast networks.
Max parallel layer uploads per push.
Max retries per layer pull on transient errors.
Default shutdown grace before SIGKILL on daemon stop.
Daemon log level. `debug` for verbose troubleshooting (also `debug: true` shortcut).
Daemon log output format: `text` or `json`.
Shortcut for `log-level: debug`. Setting via daemon.json + SIGHUP is the recommended way to flip on debug logs without a full restart.
Daemon-level labels (`key=value`). Surfaced in `docker info`. Used by orchestrators to schedule based on host attributes.
Runtime exec options. e.g. `["native.cgroupdriver=systemd"]` to make the daemon use systemd as the cgroup driver — required for kubelet integration on systemd hosts.
CDI spec directories. Used for vendored device drivers (NVIDIA via CDI).
Daemon's own OOM-killer preference. Set to -500 to keep dockerd alive when host is under memory pressure.
CPU real-time runtime budget for the parent cgroup. Cgroup v1 only.
CPU real-time period for the parent cgroup. Cgroup v1 only.
Default swarm advertise interface/address. Swarm-only; otherwise irrelevant.
Legacy KV store for swarm classic. Effectively dead key on modern installs.
Legacy swarm advertise.
Legacy swarm KV options.
Names of authorization plugins (volume / log / network / authz extensions). Daemon refuses ops not allowed by all listed plugins.
Run dockerd in rootless mode (typically launched by RootlessKit). Detail in docker/security; here just the daemon-level toggle.
`dockerd --validate` checks the daemon config and exits without starting. Use in CI before rolling new daemon.json into prod.
Emit timestamps without ANSI colors (logs to journals/files cleanly).
CLI-form `--feature key=true` equivalent of `features` map.
User-defined resources advertised by the swarm node (e.g. `["GPU=UUID1","GPU=UUID2"]`).
MTU for the swarm control-plane.
Default gateway IPv4 for the default bridge.
Default gateway IPv6 for the default bridge.
Host IP for port publishing from the default bridge. Pin to a single interface to avoid binding to all.
Don't set the FORWARD chain default to DROP when enabling IP forwarding.
Network bridge interface name to attach containers to.
IPv4 subnet allocated for default bridge containers (within `bip`).
Daemon-wide default for the no-new-privileges security flag on new containers.
Verbose mount syntax. Required for volume-driver options, volume-subpath, and bind-create-src. See `mount-spec` scope for sub-keys.
Daemon-managed restart policy. `unless-stopped` ≈ `always` but doesn't restart after explicit `docker stop`.
Per-container logging driver. Override of daemon-default. Re-creating the container is required to change.
Per-container log driver options.
Add a Linux capability. Common: NET_ADMIN (tcpdump), SYS_PTRACE (strace), SYS_ADMIN (mounts), NET_RAW (ping).
Drop a Linux capability. `--cap-drop=ALL` + selective `--cap-add` is the least-privilege baseline.
Security options. Common: `seccomp=<file>|unconfined`, `apparmor=<profile>`, `label=<…>`, `no-new-privileges:true`.
Set ulimits in the container. e.g. `--ulimit nofile=65536:65536`. Daemon default via `default-ulimits`.
Hard memory limit. Hitting it triggers OOM-killer; container exits with code 137. Always set in production.
Memory + swap limit. Set to -1 for unlimited swap. Must be ≥ --memory.
Tune kernel swappiness for the container.
Memory soft limit. Kernel attempts to keep below; doesn't OOM-kill.
CPU quota expressed as fractional cores. Translates to `cpu-period`/`cpu-quota` cgroup knobs.
Relative CPU weight under contention. 1024 = baseline. NOT a hard cap.
CPUs to allow execution on. e.g. `0-3` or `0,2`. Pinning for NUMA / latency-sensitive workloads.
NUMA memory nodes the container can allocate from.
CFS period (default 100000μs = 100ms). Combined with --cpu-quota = hard CPU cap.
CFS quota in microseconds. With period 100k, quota 50k = 0.5 CPUs.
Network to attach. Names of `docker network ls` rows, or `host` (no isolation), `none`, `container:<id>` (share another container's net ns).
PID namespace mode. `host` (host pid ns — see all host processes), `container:<id>` (share another container's pid ns — debug-sidecar pattern). Combined with --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE for strace/gdb.
IPC namespace mode: host|container:<id>|private|shareable|none. `shareable` (default) lets `--ipc=container:` work later.
User namespace mode. Only valid value is `host` — disables daemon-wide userns-remap for this container.
Cgroup namespace mode.
UTS namespace. Only `host` allowed. Disallows --hostname/--domainname when host.
GPU pass-through. `all` for every GPU; `device=0,1` for specific. Requires NVIDIA Container Toolkit + nvidia runtime.
All capabilities + host devices + AppArmor/seccomp disabled. Effectively root-on-host. Avoid; use targeted --cap-add and --device.
Mount root fs read-only. Combine with `--tmpfs /tmp` etc. for writable scratch. Hardening best-practice for stateless services.
Inject docker-init/tini as pid 1. Forwards signals + reaps zombies. Fixes 'docker stop hangs' and zombie process leaks.
Size of /dev/shm.
Health-check shell command. Combine with --health-interval / --health-retries / --health-start-period.
Time between health checks.
Consecutive failures before marking unhealthy.
Max time per probe.
Initial wait before counting failures. Lets the app start without flapping unhealthy.
Health-check cadence during the start period.
Pass a host device through (e.g. `/dev/sda`, `/dev/nvidia0`).
Add a rule to the cgroup devices allowlist (e.g. `c 1:3 mr` allow read/mknod on /dev/null major:minor).
Mount volumes from another container (legacy data-container pattern). See container-run --volumes-from in docker-docs-storage-volumes.
Initial working directory.
User to run as: `<uid>` or `<name>`, optionally `:<gid|group>`. Override image USER.
Override the image's ENTRYPOINT. `--entrypoint=sh` is the canonical way to shell into a broken image.
Load env vars from KEY=VALUE files.
Set metadata labels on the container.
Read labels from a file (one per line).
OCI runtime for this container (runc | crun | io.containerd.kata.v2 | …).
Force platform on multi-arch images. e.g. `linux/amd64`.
When to pull. `always` for fresh-bytes guarantees, `never` for air-gapped.
Signal sent on `docker stop`.
Grace period before SIGKILL.
Container-level pids cgroup limit. -1 also = unlimited. Defense against fork bombs / leaked-process accumulation.
Set sysctls inside the container's namespaces. Only namespaced sysctls are settable (e.g. `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`).
Mount a tmpfs at the given path. Default tmpfs opts: `rw,noexec,nosuid,size=65536k`. Combine with --read-only for safe scratch space.
Max single log file size before rotation. e.g. `10m`. THE knob to set — without it, json-file fills the disk on long-running containers.
Number of rotated files kept. Only effective with max-size set.
Compress rotated logs (gzip).
Daemon-wide allowlist of label keys included in log entries.
Regex form of `labels`.
Env-var keys included in log entries.
Regex form of `env`.
Tag template for log entries. Supports `{{.ID}}`, `{{.FullID}}`, `{{.Name}}`, `{{.ImageName}}`.
Fluentd collector socket. tcp://host:24224 or unix:///path/to/fluentd.sock. tcp default scheme.
If false, container fails to start when fluentd unreachable. true = fire-and-forget with buffer.
Reconnect interval (ms) when async. Useful when address is a Consul service that resolves multiple IPs.
In-memory buffer size (events). Full buffer = call to write logs fails.
Sleep between retries.
Max retries (default = max uint32). Set lower to fail fast.
Emit nanosecond-precision event timestamps.
Write-call timeout to fluentd daemon. Default = block forever — set this in production.
Per-message tag template. e.g. `docker.{{.Name}}`.
Sets `CONTAINER_TAG` and `SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER` in the journal entry.
Comma-separated label keys included as journal fields.
Regex form.
Comma-separated env keys to include.
Regex form.
Syslog endpoint. Forms: tcp://host:514, udp://host:514, tcp+tls://host:514, unix:///dev/log.
RFC 5424 facility (daemon, local0..local7, etc.).
CA cert for TLS-syslog.
Client cert for TLS-syslog.
Client key for TLS-syslog.
Wire format. rfc5424 has structured-data, rfc3164 is BSD legacy.
Max single log file size. Local driver rotates by default.
Number of rotated files kept.
Compress rotated files.
GELF endpoint. udp://host:12201 or tcp://host:12201.
Compression for UDP GELF. Set `none` for low-CPU/MTU-tuned setups.
Max TCP reconnect attempts.
Delay between TCP reconnect attempts.
Tag template for GELF messages.
Mount type. cluster = swarm-only.
For volume = volume name (omit for anonymous); for bind = host path; for tmpfs = unused.
Container path (must be absolute).
Mount read-only inside the container.
Bind-mount propagation. r-prefixed = recursive. shared = sub-mounts in either direction propagate. Detail in docker-docs-storage-bind-mounts.
Don't include host sub-mounts in the container's view.
Recursive bind behavior. `readonly` requires kernel ≥ 5.12; older kernels = read-write submounts.
Auto-create source path if it doesn't exist (matches `-v` legacy behavior). Default `--mount` errors out — use this opt-in to mirror -v.
Volume driver (e.g. `local`, `rclone`).
Volume-driver options. e.g. for local + nfs: `volume-opt=type=nfs,volume-opt=device=…,volume-opt=o=addr=…`.
Don't copy container's pre-existing dir contents into a new volume.
Mount only a subdirectory of the volume into the container. Subdir must exist or mount fails.
Tmpfs upper bound.
Tmpfs file mode bits.
macOS-only. Tunes filesystem coherence vs perf for Docker Desktop bind mounts.
CLI's daemon address. ssh://user@host accepted; password auth NOT supported (must use ssh-agent / passwordless key).
Equivalent to --tlsverify.
Dir containing ca.pem, cert.pem, key.pem.
Override CLI config dir (auths, contexts, plugins).
Toggle BuildKit for `docker build`. Detail in docker/build-buildkit.
Pick a docker context for one command. Beats setting DOCKER_HOST manually per shell.
Pin the API version. Useful for ABI-tied scripts.
Default platform for `docker pull` / `docker build` / `docker run`. e.g. `linux/amd64`.
Proxy used by both daemon and CLI for HTTP traffic (registry pulls, registry push). Honored by daemon when started with this in env (systemd drop-in convention).
HTTPS proxy. Takes precedence over HTTP_PROXY for https URLs (Go http.proxy semantics).
Hosts/CIDRs/wildcards to skip proxying. Forms: `1.2.3.4`, `1.2.3.4:80`, `example.com`, `.example.com`, `*`, comma-separated.
Bypass overlay2 kernel-version check. Use only if you know your kernel supports OverlayFS but reports an older version (back-ported, e.g. RHEL 3.10.0-514).
Per-container quota for overlay2 upperdir. Requires xfs+pquota or similar. Hard cap on writable-layer growth.
devicemapper-thinpool legacy: base device size for new containers.
devicemapper: explicit thin-pool device path.
ZFS dataset for daemon storage. Override for non-default ZFS layout.
btrfs: minimum free space to keep on the volume; daemon refuses to create new layers below the threshold.
